reviews.review: Almost there. Pleaaaaase just remove the pausing for upgrading. Relegate upgrade selections for loading screens or something.

Game is too easy even on high difficulty at early levels, it seems I will have to grind long ours to see more than 2 enemies next to each other, it is mostly a walking simulator at this point, definitely not a roguelike experience, where it is expected that you die and lose, here everyone is a winner no matter what it seems.

Roguelikes, at their core, are made by gamers who just want to have their own dopamine boost. For those who want as much silly dopamine rushes as possible, even if perhaps at the cost of allowing the game to rng-fight you away from it. That's why whenever you *do* get an insane build in a roguelike it feels so vindicating - you *won* against the game. You managed to break it's rules, it feels like.

So it's baffling why this game almost goes out of it's way to *not* give you this feeling.

If you've played base DRG game, you will very quickly recognize the game gives you a gun, and 5 rng upgrades for it (that aren't typically *that* interesting even compared to the base game). Sounds *kinda* like a roguelike setup, but...... Isn't that just... Base game? You also just get your gun right away there to, and even get to *choose* it, and the much more interesting gun-specific upgrades there too? So is this not literally just... The base game, but with a needless rng element slapped on top of it? And in this game, it doesn't even let you go *PAST* that power level???

I understand the expenite upgrades are also supposed to serve as a backup power to add to it, but with how minimally the power increases from them, how far between they will be (a "high amount" of these upgrades in an entire mission would be 20ish), and how harsh the journey getting there will be, it feels less like you're actually gaining any progress and more like the game is making you "stronger" by just starting you with absolutely no power at all so you feel special when you get *anything*.

Another example of this is the trait upgrades, being your out-of-run progression system - these are similarly extremely minimal. It takes a long, LONG time to get all of them, takes money to even have the slots for them, and even when you do have a perfect build for them, you just kinda feel like you're as strong as any good overclock in the base game would be.

I genuinely just don't know who this game is for, honestly. It absolutely cannot be for DRG fans of the base game, because you are just *better* there, even without """""infinite""""" upgrades via expenite. It's significantly harder, you have way less stuff to collect and not necessarily any varying objectives makes all maps and biomes still feel same-y, and even when you start to feel like you're doing something epic with a build you finally landed, the run will likely be over within the next 5-10 minutes.

Genuinely, just go play the base game. And don't play this one.
